title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 235
paragraphs: However, some of the Hellenes who wished to gain distinction for cleverness have given an account of this water in three different ways. Two of these I do not think it worth even speaking of, except just to indicate their nature. The first says that the Etesian Winds are the cause that makes the river rise, by preventing the Nile from flowing out into the sea. But the Etesian Winds often fail, and yet the Nile still does the same work it is accustomed to do; and moreover, if these winds were the cause, all the other rivers that flow in a direction opposed to the Etesian Winds ought to have been affected in the same way as the Nile, and even more so, since they are smaller and present a feebler flow of stream. Yet there are many such rivers in Syria and many in Libya, and they are affected in no such manner as the Nile.
